correctness.rationale: With t=tan(theta) and k=min(1,h/t), the boundary is four ellipse arcs plus two chords of total length 4R sqrt(1-k²). In the clipped regime the quarter arc is the integrated norm of (t,(1-x²)^(-1/2)) on [0,k]. Its strict integrated-norm bound gives P/(4R)>sqrt(h²+alpha²)+cos(alpha), alpha=arcsin(k). The derivative has the sign of alpha cot(alpha)-h, a strictly decreasing test; the bound's minimum is at an endpoint. At h=pi/2-1 the lower endpoint bound is pi/2; monotonicity in h and the full-ellipse strict inequality give exactly the claimed minimizers. Near the axial angle, the integral in the vertical coordinate gives w and w² coefficients 2Rh(1-h) and R(2h³/3-h/2-h⁴/2), so h=1 is already a strict local maximum. The full-ellipse expansion at zero angle starts with +pi R theta²/2. At contact, the missing arc minus chord is (2R/3)(1+t²)a³+O(a⁵), a²=1-h²/t². The quotient by a³ extends analytically in a² and t; substitution into theta gives the stated 3/2 coefficient and C¹ but not C² regularity, without differentiating an arbitrary error term. Strictness is for the angle variable, not for azimuthal motion among rotationally equivalent planes. Independent high-precision diagnostics agreed; the analytic proof, not those tests, establishes the theorem.
residual_risks: No classification of all oblique stationary points; nonuniform expansions in extreme aspect ratios are outside scope.
